items.title: Layer-specific prospective scientific calibration and human-factors protocol
items.currentGap: Mechanistic plausibility, source traceability, synthetic replay, and a reproducible PBPK or PK/PD implementation do not establish patient-level accuracy, benefit, or safety. Existing gastric, fed/formulation PK, LNAA transport, PBPK, and PK/PD studies measure different links in the causal chain and do not supply one transportable universal food, protein, emptying, exposure, or motor-response coefficient.
acceptanceCriteria: A preregistered protocol defines the intended context of use, population, formulation and route, fed state, comparator, measurement schedule, endpoints, error costs, sample-size rationale, and stop rules.

Calibration, discrimination, predictive error, and uncertainty are reported on immutable held-out subject, site, or time splits with subgroup and transportability limits; pooled fit is not converted into a universal coefficient.

PBPK or joint PK/PD estimation reports platform and model version, parameter provenance, assumptions, identifiability and covariance diagnostics, predictive checks, and context-of-use credibility without treating optimizer convergence as validation.
Human-factors testing verifies that explanations do not induce medication or diet changes without clinician review.

A current ignored local outer-v4/inner-v4 development attestation with nested execution-isolation-v2 passed on a dedicated API 36 arm64 emulator and bound dirty source, isolated application identity, integration entrypoint, debug APK and byte-identical installed base APK, compiled manifest, plugin lock, observed debug-signature integrity, the exact private lease-evidence digest, seven-to-zero plugin-registry behavior, application absence before installation and removal after execution. Permissions, timezone changes, recurrence, cancellation, load/resume/account reconciliation, and pending-request counts are tested on every platform that claims scheduled delivery.

A root account-owned route registry removes every page/dialog opened by A during A→null/B, ReminderCenter fails closed without a Firebase UID and rebinds a fresh controller, controller/scope leases prevent an old dialog from writing to B, and a new account waits for any unverified old-account cancellation recovery before scheduling. Locked-screen/warm/cold physical-device taps, killed-process capture, per-occurrence identity, background actions, and accessibility announcements remain unverified.
acceptanceCriteria: UI-presenting foreground/warm response and notification-launched cold start resolve the authenticated user scope and current plan revision without putting sensitive labels, medication details, or account identifiers in payloads, routes, or logs.

A meal-log prompt opens an empty editable meal draft and an intake-log prompt opens an empty editable intake draft; neither route writes a record, infers a dose, or marks adherence before explicit confirmation.

Unknown, stale-revision, disabled, deleted, malformed, cross-user, and rapidly duplicated payloads fail closed with a neutral explanation; no claim of persistent replay prevention is made for a recurring notification payload.
Android and iOS device journeys cover locked-screen body tap, cold start, warm resume, back navigation, duplicate tap, sign-out/account switch, and accessibility announcements.

A current ignored local outer-v4/inner-v4 development attestation with nested execution-isolation-v2 passed on a dedicated API 36 arm64 emulator and bound an isolated reminder-attestation application ID and label, debug integration-test APK, byte-identical pulled installed base APK, compiled manifest, plugin lock, observed debug-signature integrity, exact private lease-evidence digest and seven-to-zero registry report. items.title: Package-scoped portable dose-evidence identity projection

items.title: Versioned upstream semantic and license drift revalidation
items.currentGap: The offline influence firewall pins reproducible upstream commits and dispositions, but it intentionally does not contact GitHub during CI. It therefore cannot report that a repository moved, archived, deleted or retargeted a tag, changed its license evidence, replaced a reviewed architecture, or published a security-relevant release after the review date. A networked refresh must propose a reviewable drift artifact without automatically rewriting the release boundary or importing upstream content. A schema-v1 metadata-only proposal collector now observes the current default-branch head, reviewed-commit resolution, tag references at that pin, repository identity, provider archive state where exposed, provider-detected SPDX, API version, rate-limit headers, and pagination status across GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket Cloud. GitHub checks pinned-commit ancestry against the observed default branch by bounded traversal of commit-parent metadata and never requests commit diffs. A manual workflow with contents:read uploads the JSON proposal as a 30-day artifact; it never mutates the inventory or downloads source trees, code, models, datasets, or reports. A schema-v1 review-decision tool now binds each human decision to canonical proposal and inventory SHA-256 values, reviewer identity, UTC time, rationale, classification, and HTTPS evidence references; a hash-chained append-only ledger retains accept, reject, defer, and revoke events. A baseline is projected only when the latest decision for every exact influence is accepted and the full chain validates, and the next proposal run requires both that projected baseline and its ledger. Hashes do not authenticate reviewers. The queue remains research_required: no baseline or decision ledger has been committed or exercised on a live proposal, declared license text is not extracted, GitLab/Bitbucket ancestry and Bitbucket archive state are unverified, and semantic impact still needs reviewer classification.
acceptanceCriteria: A networked proposal job records the previous and observed repository identity, full commit, release or tag identity, archive or move state, declared and detected license evidence, review timestamp, API version, and rate-limit or retrieval status without mutating the committed inventory.

License disappearance, NOASSERTION, repository transfer, deleted or mutable tag, history rewrite, unavailable API, partial pagination, rate limit, malformed response, and inconsistent repository metadata produce unverified or blocker status rather than pass.

A reviewer classifies whether each changed upstream alters only an observed concept, a copied or linked artifact, an obligation, a NOTICE or source offer, an SBOM component, or a scientific/model/data claim; no code, model, data, or report is downloaded into the release by this workflow.

Accepted refreshes update the pinned inventory and an append-only drift record in one reviewed change, while rejected or deferred drift leaves current release consumers blocked if their approved transfer evidence is stale.

items.title: Executable trace and visualization coverage for every algorithm claim
items.currentGap: The current worktree truthfully gives all 63 registered algorithms a searchable static visual contract and marks only fourteen IDs mechanically emitted by production-engine-derived fixed-scenario explanation trees as live. The input_quality_gate trace reports dimension statuses and the exact product-strength-only hold from the real gate result; it is explicitly a standalone synthetic assessment and does not authorize or veto the other Observatory traces. The medication_entry_validator trace exposes only structural disposition and required-field presence from the real validator result, without medication names or source identifiers; the time_axis_builder trace exposes per-type relative event offsets and counts omitted or rejected inputs without absolute timestamps or event IDs. The protein_trend node executes the existing production aggregation on three fixed synthetic meals and exposes only relative-day grams and the per-meal mean, omitting row IDs and absolute timestamps. The dosage_note_parser executes five fixed synthetic syntax cases and emits only status/reason counts; raw text and quantities are withheld, and the standalone probe does not feed other traces. The gastric_structural_uncertainty_shadow_ensemble trace executes the read-only production report on fixed synthetic scenarios and exposes observable-matched versus held trajectory counts, a short report digest, and whether the unchanged production output was preserved; unavailable profiles produce an explicit not-run state, and no shadow trajectory authorizes fitting or affects recommendations. The protein_distribution trace projects the production scorer’s existing redistribution roles and scores for fixed synthetic candidates, while withholding candidate names, identifiers, catalog references, protein grams, and absolute timestamps; it does not recompute results or affect ranking. A schema-v1 content-addressed trace-surface manifest binds these fourteen IDs to provider observatory.production-snapshot/1, synthetic fixture schema and revision, explicit eager registration and immutable-value no-disposal lifecycle, the app-tools.observatory destination, algorithm-specific UI surface keys, source ownership and executable tests; CI compares the reviewed config with the compiled registry and UI shows 14/63 production traces versus 49 static-only contracts. Generic flow contracts do not count as live. Deliberate production-trace coverage for the other 49 algorithms, target-device screen-reader and keyboard evidence, and semantic execution-path coverage remain open.
acceptanceCriteria: Every live-trace registry claim resolves to a versioned production-engine provider with explicit identifier, registration and disposal lifecycle, fixture schema, algorithm-specific widget or structured table, source path, and executable test.
All registered algorithms have either a truthful executable representation or an explicit non-executable static reason; a generic icon-only contract never counts as a live trace.
Missing providers, dead UI routes, fixture drift, and source-path mismatches fail CI.
Every complex chart has a concise semantic label, an equivalent visible long description, and a structured data-table view.

items.title: Atomic, idempotent, and resumable onboarding commit
items.currentGap: The current worktree now uses a versioned SHA-256-identified OnboardingCommit and publishes visible AppState only after persistence and account-scope revalidation. Memory swaps the complete snapshot without an await, native SQLite uses one transaction, browser storage serializes one aggregate envelope, and Firestore uses one owner-bound batch with a committed marker; conformance and injected write-before/lost-ack tests cover idempotent retry. The seven-case Firestore Emulator suite now runs locally through an auto-discovered JDK 21 and proves the owner-bound terminal onboarding marker plus adjacent allow/deny rules. Acceptance remains open because the production AppDatabase Firestore batch has not run end-to-end through Firebase Auth plus Firestore emulators or a real project, native SQLite has not run through a target-device plugin runtime, legacy partially written onboarding state has no explicit migration/repair path, browser storage has no cross-tab CAS, and simultaneous different Firestore operation IDs remain complete-state last-writer-wins rather than business-level compare-and-set.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned OnboardingCommit carries UID, schema version, and idempotency token and is applied atomically by each supported persistence backend.
Durable success precedes in-memory publication; post-commit refresh failure is reported separately from commit failure.
Injected failure at every write boundary never produces onboarded=true with required records missing, and retry never duplicates the initial intake.
Cold start and account switch can safely resume or roll back an interrupted commit, with an explicit migration strategy for existing partial states.

Cross-tab and cross-device submissions of different operation IDs have a declared conflict policy and executable CAS or intentionally reviewed last-writer behavior; a retry of the same operation never overwrites later user edits.

items.title: Registered-user first-day journey across real persistence backends
items.currentGap: The existing registered-user journey uses an ephemeral in-process service graph and can substitute test repositories, so it does not yet prove production Auth and repository wiring, a meal and intake round trip, edit/delete, offline retry, cold recovery, ownership isolation, or field fidelity across SQLite, browser storage, and Firebase emulator backends. A central checker now inventories 25 required known schema or persistence surfaces (18 versioned and 7 explicitly unversioned) and auto-discovers Dart schema URIs and named version constants, including the portable package and owner-token boundary; it cannot infer an entirely new unmarked persistence write or prove migration and deployed-backend compatibility. The dashboard also lacks a state-derived, non-prescriptive first-day checklist.
acceptanceCriteria: A dismissible checklist derived from durable state guides confirmation of selected medication, explicit intake and meal creation, trace viewing, edit, and delete without auto-writing records or prescribing medication, timing, or diet.

Canonical post-registration journeys run through production Auth and repository boundaries against temporary SQLite, real browser storage, and Firebase Auth plus Firestore emulators without test-only repository substitution, then recover through a cold new service graph.

Each backend journey covers registration, explicit meal and intake creation, trace view, edit, delete, offline or interrupted write and retry, restart, sign-out, and account switch, and distinguishes infrastructure failure from product failure.
Records restore only for the owning account and preserve timestamps, units, null-versus-zero meaning, provenance, reminder state, and audit links across backends.
The schema catalog enumerates every persisted boundary and its checker fails when a production persistence surface is missing from the catalog.

items.title: Medication assertion source and temporal reconciliation
items.currentGap: Implemented in the current worktree: Intake schema v3 retains bounded immutable medication assertions and append-only decisions, including a local source-class analogue of FHIR MedicationStatement informationSource; each node carries an effective interval, explicit time precision and a not taken state; the conflict graph retains clock skew and retraction rather than overwriting them; and the resolver never infers adherence or makes a FHIR conformance claim. SQLite v10, Web/Firestore, recovery and portable JSON paths preserve the envelope; all main result-affecting dose paths now require one exact active local receipt, a non-conflicting graph and an as-of observation boundary. Evidence confirmed, asserted, recorded, imported or reconciled after the requested observation is held rather than leaked backward. A read-only `projectBitemporal(validAt, knownAt)` API now emits a deterministic schema-v3 evidence projection that keeps the clinical interval separate from the knowledge cutoff, withholds post-cutoff claim and decision payloads, and leaves the dose-result gate closed to projection output. Timeline exposes a responsive English/Chinese source-and-conflict review; malformed evidence is quarantined rather than crashing or becoming absence; and the independent mutation gate remains part of the verifier. The local source-review page now exposes UTC valid-time and knowledge-time cutoffs, hides later claim/decision details, and invalidates a projection when its graph revision changes. Schema-v3 binds a conflict graph rebuilt only from cutoff-visible assertions and decisions, using validAt for temporal edges; aggregate integrity markers with no independent knowledge timestamp are marked unresolved at the cutoff, excluded from the historical graph, and surfaced as an incomplete projection; the view has no dose-eligibility field and does not alter the current result gate. Medication assertion schema v2 now persists an optional bounded user-entered source display label, binds new labeled assertions to that label, preserves v1 identity digests without inventing labels, and shows source names in the current and cutoff-visible relationship views. The visit-preparation report now carries blocking relationships and integrity findings from a cutoff-bound projection, readable source labels or evidence-class fallbacks, source-claimed dose/status/time fields, and any owner-recorded review choice; caps and omitted-record counts are explicit, and acknowledgements leave conflicts intact. This remains a visit discussion aid, not clinical reconciliation. The preview now links each displayed intake issue to the current source-review page, rechecks account ownership before navigation, and labels the destination as current because evidence may have changed since report generation. The label is still only user-entered metadata, not issuer verification. This is an API and UI slice, not a complete bitemporal subsystem. Remaining research and external-validation gaps include governed transaction-time semantics, durable observation-time capture for future aggregate integrity markers; existing untimed markers cannot be dated retroactively, issuer authenticity and trust policy, frequency and multi-dose course semantics, real cross-device/offline concurrency, full translated copy for every locale, representative-user usability, clinician-led reconciliation evaluation and Parkinson-specific performance. FHIR mappings remain inspiration only, and acknowledgement cannot release an unresolved conflict.
acceptanceCriteria: Every assertion is immutable and binds medication, product, dose, route/form/release, source class, source artifact and revision digest, asserting actor/role, derivation links, effective time or interval, precision and uncertainty, asserted/imported/recorded clocks, status (taken, not taken, unknown or entered in error), owner scope and schema identity; an optional bounded user-entered source display label is preserved and identity-bound in v2, while v1 remains unnamed with its original identity; absence remains unknown and no source is relabelled as formal administration.

A deterministic conflict graph retains patient, caregiver, package, device, imported statement, prescription, dispense and formal administration claims separately; duplicate, stale, superseded, retracted, future-dated, time-zone ambiguous, partially overlapping and dose/frequency/product-conflicting claims remain enumerable instead of being silently overwritten or resolved by a universal source hierarchy.

Result-affecting algorithms receive a dose only from an exact current local confirmation whose source chain is non-conflicting for that event; the resolver never infers adherence, actual administration, prescription validity or clinician agreement from a record, dispense, bottle, device or absence of contradiction.

A nontechnical accessible reconciliation UI shows side-by-side source, event time, assertion time, import time, precision, changed fields and evidence availability; user acknowledgement appends a decision without deleting prior claims, and every shipped locale supports keyboard, screen reader, zoom and reflow review.

Portable export and audit preserve the complete local conflict and decision graph with FHIR-inspired mapping notes but no FHIR conformance claim; independent mutation, property, restart, offline, cross-device and cross-account tests cover source substitution, delayed import, clock skew, DST ambiguity, duplicate events, status inversion, retraction erasure, dangling derivation, stale reconciliation and acknowledgement loss, while representative-user and clinician-led studies are required before any medication-safety or reconciliation-effectiveness claim.

items.title: FHIR, UCUM, and RxNorm structured medication-dose semantic profile
items.currentGap: The current grammar, confirmation receipt, package-dose calculator, metadata completeness gate, input-quality gate and medication-assertion graph keep a locally typed administration quantity separate from product strength and fail closed for selected ambiguity, non-finite, non-positive, overflow, stale, future and conflicting cases. A source-pinned, SHA-256 content-addressed metadata manifest now identifies NLM's 2026-09-08 RxNorm Current Prescribable Content release, including filename, publisher MD5, official release-note scope and terms. The archive was not downloaded or locally checksum-verified, no RXCUI/product mappings are shipped, and absence from the active subset remains unresolved rather than retired. An opt-in diagnostics lookup now sends two manually entered names to the exact RxNav approximate-term endpoint only after separate consent; it displays at most 20 named active RXNORM-source candidates, preserves lexical rank as ordering only, discards match score, and does not automatically select a candidate or feed a rule. After candidate discovery, the user may choose two query-safe RxNorm display strings and separately consent to a distinct openFDA label-text search; that request sends neither RxCUI nor the original typed names, and its literal label evidence does not feed a clinical rule. A further consented action previews current name, TTY, synonym, language, and suppression properties for one recently returned RxCUI; it remains page-memory metadata, not a pinned terminology row, user-medication confirmation, product mapping, or rule input. A development-only preview (schema parkinsum.fhir-r5-dose-quantity-preview/2) projects one exact, confirmed local administration quantity to an offline FHIR R5 Dosage doseQuantity fragment for four UCUM code identifiers (mg, g, ug, mL), with a content-addressed resource_or_exchange_eligible=false contract. The saved-intake timeline now exposes a user-triggered, owner-scope-rechecked read-only dialog that shows only an eligible quantity and lists unprojected local medication fields; it has no copy, save, send, or algorithm-input path. Its schema-v2 path ledger classifies FHIR R5 Dosage elements with field dispositions of mapped, partially mapped, unsupported or not projected, including the one-entry doseAndRate bound, dose Range, all rate alternatives, Timing, maxima, route, method and extensions. Dosage.text represents only a partial dose token, not a full SIG, and the ledger does not validate nested datatypes or a complete profile; it creates no Medication resource and does not perform independent FHIR R5 validation, full-profile validation, RxNorm mapping or clinical interpretation. The broader profile still lacks a pinned FHIR R5 profile and validator package, reviewed UCUM release or subset, and governed algorithm identity binding. There is no governed derivation proving when a confirmed package count and Medication ingredient strength may yield an administration quantity, no explicit concentration bridge for mass-to-volume transformation, and no full Medication-resource mapping, independent import/export validator, or round-trip evidence; the path ledger covers only the bounded Dosage fragment. The development-only schema parkinsum.fhir-r5-medication-product-preview/3 still projects product and ingredient text only from the existing FhirInspired view. An opt-in MedicationProductPack path adds strengthQuantity only for an exact source strength lexeme whose parsed positive numerator matches, whose unit is exactly g, mg or ug, whose source URL is host-checked against a supported openFDA or Health Canada importer, whose source denominator is absent or numeric one without a unit, and whose dosage form is exactly tablet. The openFDA path additionally requires a unique exact match to the content-addressed bundled source manifest and binds asset SHA-256, product NDC, product ID, SPL ID, ingredient index/name, parser-result SHA-256 and source-row SHA-256 into the preview digest; this local byte-identity match does not verify FDA data truth or currentness. Health Canada remains host-checked without an equivalent bundled row manifest. Other forms, concentration denominators, explicit denominator units, unsupported units, missing or mismatched lexemes, and unrecognized source hosts remain local evidence. The schema-v3 profile manifest references FHIR Core 5.0.0 and UCUM 2.2/license 1.1 but does not redistribute UCUM tables or parser code or establish license clearance. This bounded Quantity projection remains a partial development preview, not a complete Medication resource/profile or validator result, and is ineligible for exchange, administration-dose derivation, receipts, or algorithms. FHIR-shaped, UCUM-shaped or RXCUI-bearing data therefore remains result-ineligible without exact local confirmation and conflict-free provenance; structural standards conformance cannot establish dose appropriateness, actual administration, adherence, prescription validity or clinical correctness. A development-only `parkinsum.openfda-strength-expression-parse-result/1` contract with a schema-v1 openFDA NDC strength-expression parser now preserves the exact source string and anchored decimal/unit lexemes for all 213 ingredient rows across 157 records in the 2026-08-17 local snapshot (SHA-256 8b2e38710abe34567414c66bd5c1a197e74b256da1b16d7d7a947fad554f063c). A bare /1 remains a denominator numeral without a unit; /5mL and /24h remain unresolved unit-bearing text, with no conversion or rate/concentration classification. Every result is held, content-addresses the parser version and exact expression, and is ineligible for UCUM mapping, FHIR strength, administration dose, and algorithm use; a separate `parkinsum.openfda-strength-expression-source-manifest/1` now binds each row to product NDC, product ID, SPL ID, ingredient index/name, and the exact source asset digest, but does not establish FDA verification. CDSS-117 adds a local schema-v1 MedicationPackageDoseDerivation snapshot to the existing product-to-quantity path. It binds source system, source URL, retrieval time, exact strength text, parsed numerator and denominator, the explicit or assumed one-tablet/capsule/caplet basis, confirmed unit quantity, formula identity and result into the product snapshot digest covered by the existing administration-dose receipt. The calculator now holds liquid, volume-denominator, unsupported-form and mismatched-unit cases; the UI displays the source and arithmetic and flags an assumed denominator before confirmation. This bounded trace does not verify the source record or its currentness, establish FDA/Health Canada semantics, assign UCUM meaning, or qualify result use. The separate lexical parser remains research-only and does not supply the calculator. Full raw-source content identity, reviewed strength semantics, RxNorm mappings, FHIR profile validation, terminology governance and algorithm identity binding remain open. A separately consented, candidate-specific RxNav history/status preview can inspect one RxCUI returned by the latest RxNorm name search; historical statuses remain descriptive and any remapped RxCUIs stay unselected candidates, with no auto-follow, medication substitution, confirmation, persistence or algorithm input.
acceptanceCriteria: A content-addressed profile manifest pins FHIR R5 hl7.fhir.core#5.0.0, every constrained profile and validator package, a reviewed UCUM release or explicitly bounded subset plus license disposition, and an exact RxNorm full or Current Prescribable Content release filename, date, checksum, release notes, source scope and terms; any version or license change alters governed configuration, event-ledger, replay and export identities and opens requalification.

Until terminology rows are governed for use, a versioned SHA-256 manifest binds the exact RxNorm Current Prescribable Content filename, release date, publisher checksum, release-note scope and terms; an unverified archive checksum stays labeled unverified, absence remains unresolved rather than retired, and release drift holds for review.

The structured model and UI keep raw instructions, Dosage.doseAndRate.dose[x] medication amount per administration, dose range, rate, Timing, maximum dose, route and method separate from Medication ingredient.strength[x], total package amount, package count, dose form, release identity and individual ingredients. Product or ingredient strength never becomes an administration dose without an explicit confirmed quantity, denominator, derivation formula, source chain and receipt.

Every computable quantity preserves value, implicit precision, comparator where the selected datatype permits it, human-readable unit, terminology system, machine code, original value, canonical value, dimension, conversion identity and held reason. Only reviewed commensurable same-dimension UCUM conversions execute; display text is never used as a code, and mass-volume conversion remains held unless an explicit current concentration ratio and package context provide a governed bridge. Non-finite, non-positive, overflow, ambiguous, stale, unsupported or dimensionally invalid values cannot affect a result.

Every medication mapping binds RXCUI, RxNorm term type, source vocabulary, release, active or retired state, ingredient, strength, dose form, branded or clinical-drug granularity, jurisdiction and license boundary. Renamed, merged, retired, split, weekly-updated, stale, absent or granularity-conflicting concepts append a reviewable state and remain result-ineligible; an RXCUI or successful terminology lookup cannot establish prescription validity, administration, adherence, semantic correctness or clinical appropriateness.

FHIR import and export validation emits a complete mapped, held, unsupported and lossy-field manifest for Range, Ratio, Timing, rate, maxima, route, form, release, extensions, unknown codes and source provenance. The accessible Algorithm Observatory and record-review UI show raw and canonical quantities, unit system and code, RxNorm identity and release, derivation graph, confirmation and conflict status, and every hold. Independent differential, property, round-trip, restart, cross-account, cross-release and mutation evidence covers strength-as-dose, display-as-code, unit case, missing system, terminology retirement, package-denominator drift, mass-volume substitution, dropped Range or Timing, stale confirmation and conflicting assertion sources; profile validation is never labelled clinical validation or proof that medication was taken.

Historical terminology status is shown only after separate user consent for one recent candidate; replacement RxCUIs remain unselected candidates and never update medication identity, records, or algorithm inputs.

A user-triggered offline timeline preview shows a quantity only after owner-bound dose confirmation and medication-assertion rechecks pass; held records reveal no numeric dose, the display identifies itself as partial and lists unprojected local medication fields, and the preview cannot be copied, saved, sent, or used as an algorithm input.

items.title: External medication assertion authenticity and purpose-bound trust registry
items.currentGap: The new assertion graph content-addresses source artifacts, revisions, actors and roles, but those are self-described local fields rather than cryptographic authenticity or authorization evidence. A matching digest detects later mutation only after capture; it does not prove who issued the source, whether a verifier used the correct key and canonicalization, whether the credential is expired or revoked, whether a rotated key remains valid, or whether the issuer is trusted for medication data in this jurisdiction and purpose. HL7 FHIR R5 Provenance offers target/version/agent/activity/recorded-time and optional signature structure, while AuditEvent separates operational access and security events. W3C Verifiable Credentials 2.0 supports tamper-evident issuer claims but explicitly leaves issuer trust and purpose to verifier policy and does not imply transitive trust. ParkinSUM therefore keeps every external claim result-ineligible until cryptographic verification, issuer policy and clinical meaning are represented as separate fail-closed states.
acceptanceCriteria: An immutable verification receipt binds the exact assertion and artifact digests, proof suite and canonicalization versions, issuer and key identifiers, verifier identity and time, key-validity interval, credential-status evidence and freshness, trust-policy digest, jurisdiction, purpose and a bounded machine-readable outcome; no raw private key, token or patient identifier is stored.

Cryptographic integrity, issuer authorization and clinical meaning remain three separate states. A valid signature cannot establish medication truth, administration, adherence, prescription validity, semantic correctness or permission to affect an algorithm, and unsupported proof suites or unknown issuers fail closed.

Revocation, expiry, stale status, key rotation, issuer-policy change, verifier-version change and credential supersession append new decisions and invalidate prior eligibility without deleting the assertion or rewriting the historical verification record.

A nontechnical accessible UI shows issuer, key, proof method, checked time, status freshness, revocation and policy result independently; it never uses one green badge to imply authenticity, authority and clinical correctness together, and every shipped locale supports keyboard, screen reader, zoom and reflow review.

Independent tamper, wrong-key, wrong-issuer, unsupported-suite, expired, revoked, stale-status, rotated-key, policy-change, offline, cross-account and replay mutations plus an external security review are required before any externally sourced medication assertion can become result-eligible; implementation must avoid FHIR, VC or non-repudiation conformance claims without the relevant test suite and governance evidence.

items.title: Versioned local dose-unit mapping provenance and eligibility gate
items.currentGap: The parser previously reduced several user-entered dose-unit spellings and mass conversions to a local unit code without preserving the exact mapping evidence that authorized the conversion.
acceptanceCriteria: Every accepted token in the closed ParkinSUM dose vocabulary carries source and canonical system URIs, codes, displays and terminology versions, a grammar source revision, exact mapping type, explicitly not-applicable local jurisdiction, review date, and local-authored license disposition.

Only exact, same-dimension conversions with positive integer rational factors can produce a canonical value; unknown, approximate, ambiguous, stale, unlicensed, malformed, dimensionally invalid, or revision-drifted mappings stay unmapped and cannot affect a dose result.

The exact mapping evidence is bound into the user confirmation receipt and portable export, while the versioned unit contract enters canonical algorithm configuration and its event-ledger configuration identity.
The implementation is limited to ParkinSUM's local dose-token vocabulary and claims no UCUM, RxNorm, RxClass, SNOMED, INFOODS, FHIR, prescription, or clinical conformance.

items.title: Versioned clinical and nutrition terminology firewall
items.currentGap: The worktree now has one bounded versioned mapping contract for user-entered local dose tokens, and the bounded FHIR R4 blood-pressure mapper emits LOINC Coding.version 2.83 from the current official release. The mapper pins UCUM specification 2.2 locally, but FHIR R4 Quantity has no terminology-version field, so the UCUM release is not carried on the wire and no UCUM terminology validation is claimed. The project does not include UCUM tables or a parser, nor the broader clinical/nutrition assets. Other FHIR views remain intentionally inspired projections. A local exact conversion cannot supply external terminology equivalence or make an incomplete source mapping result-safe.
acceptanceCriteria: Every result-affecting drug, ingredient, product, formulation, route, food component, and unit mapping records system URI, code, display, terminology version, source revision, mapping type, jurisdiction, review date, and license state.

Original and canonical UCUM units plus explicit conversion factors are preserved; dimensionally invalid, ambiguous, approximate, stale, or unlicensed mappings remain unmapped and cannot influence an algorithm.

RxNorm, RxClass, SNOMED, INFOODS, UCUM, and FHIR assets retain separate license and version boundaries; FHIR-inspired projections cannot be labelled conformant without a pinned profile and validator evidence.

The bounded FHIR R4 blood-pressure mapper emits the LOINC code-system version on each panel/component Coding and records the local UCUM release boundary; the standard Quantity wire shape is not extended with an invented terminology-version field.
Terminology and conversion versions enter portable exports, event-ledger identity, and canonical algorithm configuration; unknown never becomes zero or a guessed equivalent.

items.title: Cross-backend durable mutation protocol
items.currentGap: The worktree now gives meal and intake create, update, delete, and restore a schema-v1 operation ID, canonical before/after payload digest, compare-and-set conflict, idempotent retry, and record-plus-revision atomic boundary in memory, the Web aggregate envelope, native SQLite, and Firestore transactions. Focused tests cover stale writes, restart restore, idempotency, legacy Web migration, SQLite rollback, and Firestore owner/schema/append-only semantics. The broader protocol remains open: profile, medication selection, preferences, reminders, and other ordinary mutations do not share this contract; owner scope is inherited from the selected backend rather than bound inside each revision; Web still uses SharedPreferences without critical-data, two-tab, or process-crash guarantees; and cold acknowledgement-loss plus real two-device conflicts are unproved.
acceptanceCriteria: Every durable mutation carries owner scope, operation ID, expected revision or base digest, schema version, payload digest, and audit intent; same-operation retry is idempotent and a different-revision conflict is explicit.

SQLite uses a transaction, critical Web state uses transactional storage rather than SharedPreferences durability claims, and Firestore uses side-effect-free compare-and-set transactions with durable acknowledgement before success UI or in-memory publication.
Business state and success audit history commit in one atomic boundary, while failed, superseded, conflicted, and acknowledgement-lost outcomes remain distinguishable after a cold restart.
A shared fault matrix injects read, write, acknowledgement, quota, corruption, migration, process-kill, two-tab, and two-device interleavings and exposes only the complete old or complete new state.

items.title: Date-bounded, user-reviewed personal log handoff summary
items.currentGap: The portable package remains a machine-oriented JSON snapshot and explicitly not a clinical record. The worktree now adds an account-bound, date-bounded personal-log summary with user-selected sections and redaction, deterministic source/content digests, current-versus-historical medication separation, explicit missingness and units, the same fixed page widget for preview and raster PDF rendering, a versioned semantic-document schema v1 for headings, paragraphs, warnings, and lists, a self-contained offline HTML export, selectable structured preview, copy, print, PDF sharing, HTML file sharing through share_plus 13.3.0, and stale-source/account authorization checks. Public envelope schema v2 still separates parseable dose evidence from result eligibility and emits canonical dose only after confirmation-receipt, conflict-free assertion-graph, and artifact as-of checks; unconfirmed, stale, conflicted and future evidence remains held. Focused service and widget tests cover dose truth boundaries, markup escaping, same-ID content drift and A-to-B account interleavings. acceptanceCriteria: The user explicitly selects a date range, sections, and redaction level and previews the exact rendered output; current medications and medications referenced only by historical intakes remain distinct; personal observations are a separate opt-in section that is off by default and is previewed before sharing.

Null, zero, unknown, original timestamp and timezone, original and canonical units, source, provenance, parseable-versus-result-eligible dose state, held reasons, and unsupported-field status remain explicit; canonical dose is unavailable unless confirmation, assertion, and as-of gates pass, and selected personal observations also preserve occurrence and entry timestamps, original timezone, source, status, entered values, units and posture; redaction controls notes; the summary never infers a trend, diagnosis, threshold interpretation, treatment response, or causal relationship, fills missing data, or adds a new algorithm ranking or recommendation.

Generation, preview, copy, print, and save are bound to one owner lease plus a record-revision digest, and any account or source-state change invalidates the artifact before an irreversible side effect.

Every artifact visibly states that it is a user-entered personal log, has not been clinically verified, and is not a medical record, diagnosis, treatment plan, or recommendation; incomplete rendering, unknown schema, budget failure, or sink failure produces no shareable artifact.

items.title: Accessible, searchable, multilingual document export
items.currentGap: The PDF still rasterizes the Flutter page widget. The worktree now adds a separate semantic-document schema v1 and self-contained offline HTML with selectable text and heading, paragraph, warning, list, reading-order, English document-language, and automatic direction markup, plus an in-app selectable reading preview and explicit system file sharing. The export escapes all user text, uses no remote fonts/scripts, and is derived from the same frozen owner/source-bound content digest. Linux file sharing is unsupported; share_plus uses temporary cache files, and system share results do not prove recipient receipt or saving. A visually matching image PDF must not be presented as an accessible document.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned document schema maps headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, language, reading order, bookmarks, links, and alternative text to a tagged PDF structure tree without rasterizing text or fetching fonts at runtime.

Reviewed, redistributable offline font subsets cover every supported script and bidirectional layout; missing glyphs, unsupported locale, shaping failure, fallback-font license ambiguity, or structure loss fails closed before a shareable artifact exists.

The exact-preview contract distinguishes semantic equivalence from pixel equivalence and verifies selectable/searchable text, copy order, screen-reader order, zoom and reflow, RTL, mixed-script, page breaks, and assistive-technology behavior on supported desktop and mobile targets.

An independent PDF/UA or equivalent accessibility validator plus human assistive-technology review binds the artifact checksum and reports conformance limits; a validator pass is never described as clinical, privacy, interoperability, or regulatory validation.

items.title: User-reviewed privacy-safe technical support bundle
items.currentGap: The current worktree now generates a schema-v1, user-reviewed support bundle from a fixed allowlist of build identity, coarse platform capabilities, stable diagnostic codes, and bounded governance counts. Unknown counts remain null; raw exceptions are discarded; exact-key validation, materialization budgets, privacy-pattern scanning, source-revision and account authorization leases, section selection, exact JSON preview, Copy, conservative Save or browser-download request, and checksum identity are implemented without an upload path. Acceptance remains open because signed release attestation, complete SBOM and OS inventory, physical-device and browser delivery evidence, native copy for every shipped locale, cross-isolate diagnostics revision, and a separately consented support-case workflow are not complete.
acceptanceCriteria: Only versioned whitelist fields such as build identity, platform capability, dependency versions, and stable finding codes may enter the bundle; health records, UID, email, patient ID, activation tokens, endpoints, paths, raw exceptions, and free-form logs are mechanically excluded.
The user previews the exact bundle and can deselect sections; it stays local by default and is never uploaded, attached, copied, or saved automatically.

Secret scanning plus UTF-8 byte, node, field, and time budgets run before materialization, and unknown exception types map to stable generic codes; any failed privacy or integrity gate produces no artifact.
Account epoch or diagnostics revision drift invalidates the preview, copy or save rechecks authorization immediately before the side effect, and failed delivery never claims that a file was saved.

items.title: User-controlled reproducible support-case workflow
items.currentGap: The privacy-safe support bundle captures a bounded technical snapshot, not the user's reproduction sequence or problem report. There is no explicit start and stop session, structured problem category, privacy-reviewed coarse action-code timeline, local issue preview, retention control, or separately authorized off-device destination. acceptanceCriteria: Each relation declares a deterministic source-input generator, seed and generator-version identity, supported-domain partition, explicit precondition boundary, shrink strategy, invalid-input disposition and minimum diversity budget without using real health data.

items.title: Metamorphic execution coverage, corpus promotion, and generator drift governance

A forever-frozen corpus can overfit to known fixtures, while ungoverned rotating seeds make failures irreproducible. No reviewed workflow currently separates a locked regression corpus from exploratory seeds, promotes minimized counterexamples, compares generator versions, or detects coverage and distribution drift without selecting relations on final outcomes.
acceptanceCriteria: Source and follow-up executions collect versioned production-path coverage at a stable abstraction boundary and report differential coverage per relation, partition, seed and algorithm without treating ordinary line coverage as metamorphic adequacy.

Algorithm Observatory exposes regression versus exploratory evidence, coverage deltas, generator drift, promoted counterexamples and open production-domain gaps without presenting any metric as correctness, scientific validity, clinical benefit or safety.

items.title: Algorithm sampling operational-profile and seed-budget adequacy

There is no prospectively declared operational profile, independent seed-block replication, saturation analysis, stopping rule, uncertainty interval, or privacy-preserving external profile review. acceptanceCriteria: A versioned synthetic operational-profile contract prospectively declares input features, partitions, weights, exclusions, provenance, reviewer and context of use while clearly separating test-allocation weights from observed user or population prevalence.

Coverage, HOLD rate, unique-behavior growth and fault-detection saturation are reported by relation, partition and seed block with uncertainty, and a plateau is never presented as proof that unseen failures are absent.

items.title: Privacy-bounded semantic algorithm trace taxonomy and schema migration

items.title: Crash-consistent Android attestation publication and recovery
items.currentGap: The current coordinator proves in-process ordering and suppresses final publication after release, drain or signal failure, while one atomic latest.json rename is the completion pointer. POSIX makes one directory operation atomic and serializable but does not make a sequence of pending-attestation, Markdown and latest-pointer writes crash durable; effects can be only partially persisted without file and directory synchronization. There is no versioned promotion receipt binding post-release lease evidence, no crash injection between every write, sync and rename, and no restart recovery that distinguishes the last complete run from orphan pending or final-name files.
acceptanceCriteria: A versioned promotion receipt binds the exact attestation digest, pre-release isolation digest, independently validated post-release lease-evidence digest, source and artifact identities, run identity, predecessor completion pointer, publication implementation identity and explicit released-but-not-durably-proven or crash-durable status; unknown, partial or mismatched fields fail closed.

Deterministic crash and I/O-fault injection at every write, file sync, rename, directory sync, pointer replacement and cleanup step proves restart recovery preserves the previous complete pointer, never accepts an unreferenced final-name artifact, quarantines ambiguous remnants without deleting evidence, and permits an idempotent retry only after exact identity revalidation.

All consumers and operator documentation accept only a fully validated completion pointer and receipt; a final-name attestation, successful process exit, atomic rename, emulator result or one recovered run never establishes durable release provenance, visible delivery, production eligibility or clinical validity.

items.title: Signed reviewer authority, expiry and revocation lifecycle for configuration-completeness witnesses
items.currentGap: Current checked-in deterministic completeness witnesses bind declared field, result-sink, source, configuration and dependency evidence, but reviewedAt is unsigned metadata. There is no independent reviewer authority, exact-bytes authorization envelope, signed validity window, monotonic trust policy, distinct-reviewer and distinct-key role threshold, or append-only witness/key revocation and root-recovery lifecycle. A witness can therefore report deterministic coverage without proving that an authorized review remains current.
acceptanceCriteria: A three-layer contract keeps the deterministic content-digest completeness witness, a DSSE exact-bytes authorization binding witness digest, algorithm ID, declared configuration scope and policy digest, and a versioned trust/status ledger independently inspectable. Production private keys never enter the repository or application artifact.

The policy defines a closed reviewer-role vocabulary and thresholds satisfied only by different reviewer identities and different trusted public-key bytes; duplicate signatures, aliases, one key relabelled across roles, the proposal author, or the algorithm owner cannot manufacture independence. DSSE keyid is only an unauthenticated lookup hint and never a trust decision.

Every authorization signs issuedAt, notBefore and expiresAt and is evaluated against trusted-time evidence. Signed append-only witness and key revocation events retain their predecessor chain and historical evidence; expiry, revocation, missing time integrity, or replacement never silently renews or transfers an authorization.

Trust starts from a pinned or independently distributed root, and each sequential root rotation satisfies both the currently trusted old-root threshold and the proposed new-root threshold before activation. Unknown policy, skipped version, invalid predecessor, freeze, fast-forward, stale configuration or source, split view, or rollback against retained high-water marks yields a fail-closed HOLD.

Algorithm Observatory exposes exact witness, authorization, policy, ledger and root digests; accepted distinct reviewers, roles and key digests; validity and trusted-time state; revocation/rotation lineage; replacement and limitation. Its stable states include unsigned, signature_invalid, policy_unknown, threshold_unsatisfied, not_yet_valid, expired, witness_revoked, key_revoked, clock_unverified, stale_configuration, rollback_detected and valid_for_declared_configuration_scope, which proves neither scientific correctness nor clinical validity, individual safety, regulatory clearance, or signer non-compromise.

acceptanceCriteria: A schema-v1 fixture pins FHIR R5 5.0.0 and contains one FHIR Parameters request with one synthetic PlanDefinition resource and one synthetic subject Reference; duplicate, missing, extra, or unsupported fields fail closed.

The operation response is a FHIR Parameters resource with exactly one return parameter containing one collection Bundle for the one subject; RequestOrchestration is its first entry, with a fixed unique synthetic fullUrl, exact versioned PlanDefinition canonical, matching subject, status=draft, and intent=proposal.

The fixed result has zero proposed actions and zero created or updated resources, so the fixture creates no executable request or clinical recommendation; collection request/response metadata and extra entries are rejected.

The validator CLI itself is not run by the app or default verify gate; no R5 validator result is claimed until the optional command runs with the pinned JAR and a compatible Java runtime.
The standalone offline report emits only structural counts and a fixture SHA-256 digest, omits synthetic resource and subject identifiers, and uses no network or real patient data.

These static fixture checks do not execute PlanDefinition/$apply, ActivityDefinition/$apply, PlanDefinition/$data-requirements, CQL, or a CPG engine, and do not establish general FHIR conformance, interoperability, clinical validation, safety, or effectiveness.

items.title: Local evidence-source metadata search using fielded BM25F
items.currentGap: Diagnostics now searches the existing clinical-evidence source registry with a deterministic fielded BM25F-style ranker over title, organization, source family, document type, jurisdiction, language, and license note. It displays source identity and matched terms only; the internal lexical score is not exposed. The search excludes raw payloads, external URLs, checksums, and user or Patient records, and query text is neither persisted, logged, nor sent. This is a metadata source-finding aid, not full-text or semantic retrieval, evidence grading, rule applicability, or a clinical conclusion.
acceptanceCriteria: The local diagnostics page searches only the existing clinical-evidence source registry's title, organization, source family, document type, jurisdiction, language, and license-note fields; raw payloads, URLs, checksums, account state, and Patient data are excluded from indexing.

A bounded fielded BM25F-style ranker uses fixed documented weights, returns matched query terms, orders ties by source-document ID, and rejects duplicate source IDs, empty IDs, oversized queries, excessive distinct terms, and result limits outside 1 through 20.
The UI keeps query state in memory, makes no network call, writes no query or result, and does not emit query text to logs or rule inputs.

The UI states that lexical ordering is not evidence quality or applicability and that no metadata match does not mean evidence is absent; results do not alter clinical rules, algorithm inputs, ranking, or recommendation outputs.

Unit and widget tests cover title-versus-metadata ranking, diacritic normalization, deterministic tie order, excluded raw payload and URL content, query and result bounds, route navigation, and the explicit no-match boundary.

items.title: Exact source-to-claim currency status in evidence search
items.currentGap: Evidence-source search and the offline evidence-currency registry were separate. Search result cards now join only exact source IDs and show each linked claim's source revision and locally recorded as-of status, review method, observation/review times, and update notice. No linked row is explicitly unassessed; registry-integrity failure withholds all status details. Future-observed status is unknown at an earlier as-of time and the evidence gate blocks it. This remains a local snapshot, not a live source check, evidence-quality grade, or change to search order or clinical behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Evidence search joins a source record to currency claims only when SourceDocumentRecord.sourceDocId exactly equals EvidenceCurrencyRecord.sourceId; it does not use title, URL, fuzzy text, or lexical rank to create a link.

Each linked claim is shown separately with claim ID, exact source revision, effective status at the snapshot as-of time, review method, observed-at and review-by times, and update-notice ID when present.
No exact linked registry row is shown as unassessed and does not imply current, safe, absent, or withdrawn status; a registry integrity failure withholds all claim-status details.
A status observed after the requested as-of time resolves to unknown and blocks the affected provider in the existing evidence-currency gate; the historical snapshot does not use future status.

The diagnostics UI identifies registry status as offline and recorded, explains that current status is not scientific validity or clinical applicability, and does not alter search ordering, rules, recommendations, or ranking.

Synthetic unit and widget tests cover exact and near-match IDs, multiple claim status outcomes, missing status records, registry integrity hold, future-observation cutoff, and the UI boundary; no live refresh or clinical conclusion is claimed.

items.title: Synthetic CDS Hooks prefetch missingness semantics preview
items.currentGap: The fixed per-service prefetch maps showed resources and an empty searchset, but did not contrast a satisfied single-resource read with no value against an unsatisfied key. The preview uses only fixed synthetic fixtures, issues no network or FHIR query, reads no patient data, and does not establish service authorization, rule-engine missingness behavior, or full CDS Hooks/FHIR conformance.

items.title: Portable pause/resume checkpoints for synthetic rule-test suites
items.currentGap: Synthetic rule suites had to run from the beginning, so a local run could not be interrupted and resumed with verified progress. A bounded schema-v1 checkpoint now binds the exact suite digest, selected rule-pack identity, execution mode, and ordered completed-case report digests; resume replays and verifies that prefix before continuing.
acceptanceCriteria: The exact schema-v1 checkpoint records synthetic_only=true, suite ID and content digest, selected rule-pack binding, execution mode, and an ordered completed-case prefix with SHA-256 report digests; unknown or missing fields, malformed digests, duplicates, unsupported modes, and oversized JSON fail closed.

Focused tests cover pause/resume, round-trip encoding, identity and mode mismatch, reordered or altered prefixes, and changed report digests; the checkpoint contains no case inputs or full reports.

This is a local synthetic test workflow only: no automatic durable storage, network call, patient-record read, clinical conclusion, rule activation, or claim of clinical validation is added. The medAL workflow is a design reference only; no medAL code, rule content, or case data is copied.
